reasons.C: Short declarative sentences in runs with a dry ironic twist at the end of each ('not in the best of tempers', 'if they would only agree among themselves'), mild whimsical personification, and a confiding sympathetic stance closest to the passage's movement.
reasons.D: Good genteel irony and period diction ('it knew its place', sinner vs social nuisance), but longer semicolon-joined sentences and an earnest closing plea make it more essayistic and a touch more elaborate than the passage.
reasons.B: Right register and period feel, but the irony is thin; sentences are plain, explanatory and evenly paced, lacking the passage's quick aphoristic turns.
reasons.A: Modern plain-essay voice ('over breakfast', colon-listed inventory, stacked rhetorical questions, 'Worse,'), argumentative and summarising rather than whimsical; furthest from the passage's diction and rhythm.
